channel.title: Disability Scoop – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Disability Scoop – Bias and Credibility (disabilityscoop.com)

item.title: 'It Takes A Toll.' What Happened To Families When Caregiver Pay Was Lost
item.description: During the pandemic, federal regulators allowed more flexibility for parents and spouses to provide paid care for family members. But when one state closed its offering, families were left scrambling.

item.title: Ad Campaign Implores People To Move On From 'R-Word'
item.description: With use of the word "retarded" on the rise, a new advertising campaign is urging people to leave the term in the past much like many other outdated practices that were once commonplace.

item.title: Trump Says Presidents 'Should Not Have Learning Disabilities'
item.description: President Donald Trump is taking heat after repeatedly stating that individuals with learning disabilities should be disqualified from becoming president.

item.title: When Slowing Down Can Save A Life: Training Law Enforcement To Understand Autism
item.description: In a room filled with pounding noises and clanging cowbells, sheriff's deputies learn that sometimes the best way to handle a crisis is to simply wait.

item.title: DC Schools Discriminated Against Students With Disabilities, OCR Finds
item.description: The school district, which has one of highest rates of special education complaints in the nation, often forces families to sue for their kids to receive services, the U.S. Department of Education said.

item.title: With Settlement, Lyft Pushed To Improve Accessibility
item.description: A major ride-sharing service is facing new pressure to ensure equal access for people with disabilities.

item.title: How A Trump-Backed Voting Bill Could Impact People With Disabilities
item.description: President Donald Trump says voting changes are his number one priority, but concerns are running high that his plan could make it harder for people with disabilities to cast their ballots.

item.title: More College Students Are Seeking Disability Accommodations. Why?
item.description: The number of college students who register as having a disability has increased across the country. Nowhere has that trend been more pronounced — or debated — than at Stanford University.

item.title: Social Security Eyes SSI Reforms
item.description: The Social Security Administration says a new team is working to improve the efficiency of its Supplemental Security Income program and help recipients comply with requirements.

item.title: Adidas Introduces Shoe Geared Towards Athletes With Down Syndrome
item.description: After a multiyear collaboration with individuals with Down syndrome and other disabilities, one of the world's largest footwear companies is rolling out a shoe designed to specifically meet their needs.
